name: MIC29502WU
title: MIC2915x/2930x/2950x/2975x: 1.5 A, 3 A, 5 A and 7.5 A low-dropout regulators
summary: A family of PNP-pass low-dropout regulators for 1.5 A (MIC2915x), 3 A (MIC2930x), 5 A (MIC2950x) and 7.5 A (MIC2975x), with full-load dropout of 350 mV to 425 mV typical and output accuracy of 1% at 25°C. Fixed 3.3 V, 5.0 V and 12 V versions and adjustable versions (1.25 V to 25 V, 1.240 V reference) come in TO-220, TO-263, TO-247 and TO-252, with enable and error-flag pins on the 5-pin types. Current limit, thermal shutdown, reversed-input and load-dump protection are built in. MIC29502WU is the 5 A adjustable part with EN and ADJ in the 5-lead TO-263, 50 per tube.

notes: Note 1: the figures apply to the part in its package.
Note 2: in a dual-supply system whose load returns to a negative rail, the output has to be clamped to ground with a diode.
Note 3: IFL, the full load current, is 1.5 A for MIC2915x, 3 A for MIC2930x, 5 A for MIC2950x and 7.5 A for MIC2975x.
Note 4: the temperature coefficient is the largest change of output voltage across the full temperature range, divided by that range.
Note 5: dropout is the input-to-output difference at which the output has sunk to 99% of the value it holds with VIN = VOUT + 1V.
Note 6: the ground pin current is the quiescent current; the source supplies it on top of the load current.
Note 7: measured with VIN at nominal VOUT plus 1 V (4.3 V for a 3.3 V part, 6 V for a 5 V part), using pulse testing.
Note 8: holds for VREF ≤ VOUT ≤ (VIN – 1V), 2.3V ≤ VIN ≤ 26V, 10 mA < IL ≤ IFL and TJ ≤ TJMAX.
Note 9: thermal regulation, the output change a time T after a step in dissipation with line and load effects removed; given for a 200 mA load pulse at VIN = 20V (4 W) with T = 10 ms.

Note 10: the flag thresholds are given as voltages below the nominal reference at the adjust pin, measured with a 6 V input. The output-referred threshold equals the pin value times VOUT/VREF = (R1 + R2)/R2; at VOUT = 5 V the guaranteed flag point is a drop of 95 mV × 5V/1.240V = 384 mV. As a fraction of VOUT the thresholds do not change with VOUT: the dropout warning is typically 5% below nominal and at most 7.7%.
The unit VMAX in the second reference-voltage row should read V.

Limits that hold over –40°C ≤ TJ ≤ +125°C: ΔVO/ΔT typ 20 and max 100 ppm/°C; dropout max 200, 600, 175, 600, 250, 600 and 200 mV (every dropout maximum except the 750 mV of MIC2975x at 7.5 A); ground current max 20, 35, 50 and 75 mA; current limit max 3.5, 5.0, 10.0 and 15.0 A; ground current in shutdown max 30 µA; reference voltage 1.215 to 1.265 V and 1.203 to 1.277 V; adjust pin bias current max 120 nA; flag leakage max 2.00 µA; flag VOL max 400 mV; lower threshold max 140 mV; enable pin input current max 750 µA and 4 µA; regulator output current in shutdown max 500 µA. All other limits are at +25°C.

circuits.title: Fixed output version (MIC29300-3.3)
circuits.description: A 3-pin MIC29300-3.3 turns a 5 V rail into 3.3 V for loads up to 3 A. An input capacitor sits from the 5 V input to ground, and a 10 µF tantalum capacitor holds the output stable.

circuits.title: Adjustable output version (MIC29152WD)
circuits.description: An MIC29152WD in TO-252 makes 2.5 V at up to 1.5 A from a 3.3 V input. EN is wired to IN so the regulator is always on. R1 (191 Ω, OUT to ADJ) over R2 (187 Ω, ADJ to ground) sets the output. A 10 µF tantalum capacitor is on the output and CIN on the input.

operation.text: Four current grades share one design: MIC2915x 1.5 A, MIC2930x 3 A, MIC2950x 5 A and MIC2975x 7.5 A. The last digit sets the pins: 0 is the 3-pin fixed part, 1 is fixed with EN and FLG, 2 is adjustable with EN and ADJ, 3 is adjustable with FLG and ADJ. Fixed outputs are 3.3 V, 5.0 V or 12 V. All family members use the same pinout, so a board can take a larger or smaller grade without a new layout.

The output is a PNP transistor made on a Super βeta PNP process, so dropout is set only by its low collector-emitter saturation voltage, not by a base-emitter drop as in NPN-pass designs. Typical full-load dropout runs from 350 mV to 425 mV across the family. The cost of the low dropout is base drive that varies with load; the process cuts it to about 1% of the load current.

Current limiting is linear: in overload the output current holds constant. Thermal shutdown turns the part off when the die passes +125°C. The part and its load survive input spikes from −20 V to +60 V, and with more than about 32 V on the input an overvoltage sensor switches the regulator off. The output may be driven above its set voltage without current flowing backwards. Protection also covers reversed input polarity and leads inserted the wrong way round.

MIC29xx1 and MIC29xx2 have an EN input with TTL/CMOS thresholds. Disabled, the part draws next to nothing; only microamperes of leakage flow. EN may be connected straight to a voltage of up to 30 V, and switching the regulator on takes about 20 µA into EN. Where on/off control is not needed EN may be tied to VIN.

MIC29xx1 and MIC29xx3 have an open-collector flag that watches the output and pulls low when it falls 5% under its expected value; it can sink 10 mA. A low output points to faults such as current limit or too little input voltage. The flag does not work during overtemperature shutdown. Flagged states include dropout (low input voltage), current limit, overtemperature shutdown and very high input voltage spikes.

An output capacitor is needed for stability and lowest noise, and its size follows the output current: less current allows a smaller part. Table 4-1 gives the minimum at full load. A low-ESR type is not required and aluminium electrolytics are adequate; capacitors with extremely low ESR may make the loop unstable. Tantalum is recommended where a fast load transient response matters.

When the source has a high AC impedance, a 0.1 µF capacitor from input to GND is recommended, with good characteristics above 250 kHz. If a series resistor ahead of the input takes part of the dissipation, a capacitor of 0.1 µF or more must sit right at the part, from its input to its ground.

The regulators are specified with a finite load. With too little output current, leakage takes over and the output voltage rises; Table 4-2 gives the load that swamps leakage over the whole temperature range. In the adjustable parts the divider resistors may be sized to draw this minimum where the load current varies widely.

Thermal design needs the maximum ambient temperature, the output current, the output voltage and the input voltage. Equation 4-1 gives the dissipation, with ground current taken as 1% of IOUT; Equation 4-2 then gives the heat sink needed, with TJMAX ≤ 125°C and a case-to-sink θCS of 0°C/W to 2°C/W. Where the lowest input voltage is known and well above dropout, a series resistor at the input can take part of the heat and shrink the heat sink.

operation.topic: MIC29152 in D-Pak without heat sink
operation.text: For the TO-252 on a board with 2 oz copper and 100 mm² of copper area, θJA is 56°C/W. At TA = +75°C, VIN = 3.3 V, VOUT = 2.5 V and IOUT = 1.5 A the dissipation is 1.1472 W (Equation 4-3), which would put the junction at 139.24°C (Equation 4-4), above the +125°C limit. Without a heat sink the dissipation allowed at +75°C is 0.893 W (Equation 4-5).
When the load is returned to a negative rail, a diode from the output to ground is required as a clamp.
